headline: Medium risk: shared-output and workflow assumptions are weakly evidenced; no direct injection or leakage channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between argo-workflows and awesome-python, and neither profile shows a default path where one ingests the other's outputs. Argo only lists REST/GRPC APIs and allowlisted egress; awesome-python has no I/O surfaces. The interaction pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between the two agents, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not bridge them with copy-paste of untrusted content.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
Add provenance labels to any exchanged text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show a shared workspace, shared OAuth principal, or sensitive data class overlap. Argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters with allowlisted egress, while awesome-python lists no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. With only docs-level evidence, leakage is not established.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF awesome-python is extended to read or upload files, reassess data exposure.
mitigations: Use separate service accounts.
Mount separate directories for each agent.
Avoid placing secrets in shared paths.
Review any future upload or export feature before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write capability is documented. Argo-workflows exposes APIs and allowlisted egress, but no filesystem write or git state mutation is listed; awesome-python has no I/O surfaces or concurrency model. Without a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent is given mutable OAuth scopes on a shared resource, reassess.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-owner.
Do not share a git checkout between agents.
Separate API credentials per agent.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where argo-workflows' output becomes authoritative input to awesome-python, and awesome-python is only a collection repo with no action-taking authority shown. Because the pairwise handoff is undocumented, a cascading-error pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding argo-workflows outputs directly into an action-taking agent, reassess.
IF awesome-python is repurposed to execute or publish based on upstream text, the risk changes.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any downstream action.
Require schema validation on handoff payloads.
Mark generated text as untrusted.
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. Argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters; awesome-python lists no data classes touched. With no evidence of regulated data flow, a compliance breach is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through either agent, reassess compliance.
IF retention or residency policies are added later, compare them before deployment.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document data categories before use.
Review retention settings for any new storage path.
Use region-specific deployments if regulated data appears.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for residency and retention.
